title: Batch-review parallel agent results with Jev
description: Review independent Kimi swarm results with bounded Jev questions, fit requests to the context budget, and send uncertain or failed checks to a human.

source.title: Jev Engineering: Parallel Decisions for a 300-Agent Kimi Swarm

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Editorial guide; AI-assisted drafting and technical verification

connections.step: Estimate each structured review request before choosing a chunk size
connections.why: jevtok estimates whole-request input tokens locally, which helps test whether shared evidence and per-result questions fit TypeSafe's context budget before a live call. Ricker does not mention it.
connections.limitations: Independent MIT Python package requiring Python 3.10+ and local tokenizer dependencies. Estimates follow the reviewed Jev 1.13 encoder and must be rechecked after provider changes; it does not judge results. Local counting sends no data, but the separate TypeSafe review call sends selected evidence and may incur charges.

connections.step: Compare batched versus separate Jev request accounting and latency claims
connections.why: Its published request records and report show how to measure fan-out billing and serial-call timing. This is a benchmark reference, not a Kimi adapter or a review-quality test, and Ricker does not name it.
connections.limitations: Independent MIT Python benchmark with CC0 inputs/results at the reviewed revision. Published figures use synthetic English tickets and OpenRouter's TypeSafe-compatible endpoint; separate requests were timed serially. We inspected the report but did not reproduce its live provider run, and it does not measure whether swarm outputs were judged correctly. Live reruns require provider access and incur charges.

faqs.question: Can Jev review 300 agent results in one request?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if the shared state plus the longest question fits 32k tokens and the entire request fits 64k. Estimate the real payload first; split larger sets into bounded chunks and keep one answer ID for each result.

faqs.question: Does a Jev Noul answer have a confidence score?
faqs.answer: No. Noul returns the probability of yes from 0 to 1, without a separate confidence field. Treat a value near 0.5 as ambiguous and validate any keep or requeue threshold on labeled results.

faqs.question: Should every failed swarm result be rerun automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Rerun only a result with a recoverable failure after checking its source evidence and retry budget. Send ambiguous, missing or malformed answers to review, and stop after a fixed number of attempts.

faqs.question: Is this a working Kimi Agent Swarm integration?
faqs.answer: No. The article sketches a review loop but does not document a Kimi result-export API. Supply an authorized result feed or export, then test the adapter separately before connecting a live swarm.
